According to Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, Apple is preparing major changes to its retail stores to coincide with the upcoming launch of its Home product lineup. Apple is expected to unveil updated versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K as early as this autumn, and the related changes appear to hint that a third, more important product will debut alongside them.

Apple has been sitting on a large backlog of unreleased Home products, mainly because the Siri overhaul has been delayed multiple times. Now that the Siri revamp is finally complete, we can expect to see some of these products officially launch after years without updates.

That said, previous reports have indicated that Apple would first release updated versions of the HomePod mini and Apple TV 4K, while the company's first smart home hub (also known as a HomePod or HomePad with a display) might arrive later.

However, based on the current preparations at retail stores, the smart home hub may launch simultaneously with the updated Apple TV and HomePod mini, according to the Power On newsletter:

Of course, we'll only get a definitive answer at Apple's September event. However, based on today's report, Apple's brand-new smart home hub is likely to debut alongside the updated Apple TV 4K and a HomePod mini with Siri AI support.

Summary

As a recap, Apple's smart home hub is rumoured to feature a 7-inch square display and come in two versions: one with built-in speakers, and another with magnets on the back for wall-mounting support. The product will run an all-new operating system with a home screen that supports widgets, can be used for FaceTime calls, and of course serves as a hub for all smart home accessories and Siri. The device will also feature an A18 chip built in.

Another rumour on the Home product line is that the next-generation Apple TV 4K may come with an updated Siri Remote, though specific changes remain unknown for now.

Are you interested in the new Home products? Which one are you most looking forward to? Let us know in the comments.
